description:
FILED s456ag (Opus agent AG, round 13), found while fixing the t/uni/readline.t
census drops.  PRE-EXISTING; unrelated to that fix (which was the READLINE
rebuild, and is done).

REPRO (probed, perl 5.40.3 -- perl reads L1 on every row):

    use utf8;
    my $f = "/tmp/x.txt";
    open(my $w,'>',$f) or die; print $w "L1\n"; close $w;
    open áº , '<', $f or die;   my $c = <áº >;    # perl: L1   PCL: undef
    open(áº , '<', $f) or die;  my $c = <áº >;    # perl: L1   PCL: L1     <- the PAREN form works
    open BEE, '<', $f or die; my $d = <BEE>;  # perl: L1   PCL: L1     <- ASCII works either way

THE EMISSION NAMES THE CAUSE (paren-less, non-ASCII):

    (p-open "áº " "<" $f)                 <- a STRING, where BEE gives the bare symbol BEE
    (p-readline '|áº |)                   <- right (this half is Unicode-aware)
    (p-close (p-void-ctx (|pl-áº |)))     <- a CALL to a sub named áº 

So ONE name is answered three different ways in one statement, and the two
wrong answers come from the ALL-CAPS bareword heuristic
`$sub_name =~ /^[A-Z][A-Z0-9_]*$/` (Pl/PExpr.pm ~4045 and ~4471, and the
sibling `Pl/Parser2.pm:6381`).  `áº ` (U+1EA0) IS an uppercase letter, so under
`use utf8` it is exactly as much a filehandle-shaped bareword as `BEE`, but
`[A-Z]` says no and the word falls to the "unknown bareword string" branch in
one place and the "callable" branch in the other.

THE FAMILY: this is #452 (a bareword filehandle NAME, qualified or not) and
#266 (a bare NAME is a CALL only where it is CALLABLE) meeting #418 (a
non-ASCII name is pipe-quoted).  `Pl::ExprToCL::_bareword_fh_p` and
`Pl::PExpr::_readline_bareword_name_p` are already Unicode-aware
(`[^\W\d]\w*`); these ALL-CAPS sites are the copies that were not updated with
them.

BAR: `open`/`close`/`print`/`printf`/`eof`/`binmode` with a non-ASCII bareword
handle, paren-less AND parenthesised; the ASCII inverse byte-identical; a
non-ASCII bareword that is NOT a handle (a declared sub, a constant, a
fat-comma key, a class-name invocant) unchanged -- the ALL-CAPS test decides
more than handles, so widening it is a CLASSIFIER change and owes the
gate-SET scan over both populations.  Rows beside the s456ag readline row in
Pl/t/utf8-source-01.t (which uses the PAREN form for exactly this reason).

WHERE IT BITES: perl's own t/uni/readline.t (`open áº ,'+>',$file;` at line 22)
-- two rows that used to sit behind a DROP and now run and fail honestly.

------------------------------------------------------------------------
DONE s457aj (Opus agent AJ, round 14).

THE ONE PREDICATE.  `Pl::Environment::fh_bareword_shape` -- THE shape test for
a bareword filehandle NAME since #491 -- now delegates to a new plain
`Pl::Environment::all_caps_shape`, which is the ALL-CAPS convention as a
UNICODE shape: `\A\p{Lu}[\p{Lu}\p{Nd}_]*\z`.  On a pure-ASCII name that is
IDENTICAL to the old `[A-Z][A-Z0-9_]*` by construction (`\p{Lu}` IS `[A-Z]`,
`\p{Nd}` IS `[0-9]`), so the ASCII inverse is byte-identical without measuring
it.  The source name arrives DECODED (measured with a trace: utf8 flag on),
which is what makes `\p{Lu}` the right test rather than a byte test.

SIX hand-written copies of that regex are gone.  FOUR ask the widened shape:
  * Pl/Environment.pm fh_bareword_shape  (the handle question)
  * Pl/PExpr.pm ~2960  indirect-object METHOD-name skip
  * Pl/PExpr.pm ~2987  indirect-object INVOCANT skip
  * Pl/Parser2.pm _word_is_term          (the `WORD /` term guess)
THREE keep the ASCII spelling, through a SECOND named predicate
`Pl::Environment::all_caps_call_guess`:
  * Pl/PExpr.pm ~4044 / ~4470  handle_subcalls' two string fall-throughs
  * Pl/PExpr.pm ~5843          eval-mode array-subscript autoquote

WHY THE SPLIT, and it is MEASURED, not aesthetic: the two questions' false
positives point in OPPOSITE directions.  A wrong "yes" in a HANDLE slot is
harmless (the slot admits no other reading).  A wrong "yes" in the call guess
turns a value perl PRINTS into an undefined-subroutine death -- probe 08c,
`use utf8; no strict; print "uni:", áº¸, "\n";` prints `áº¸` in perl and on the
base, and DIED with the guess widened.  (Its ASCII twin `ABC` already dies --
#266's accepted residue -- so widening would have spread a known-wrong answer
to a case that was accidentally right.)  Both predicates carry the rationale
in their POD; #852 records what a future widening owes.

MEASURED.  Probes: 15 files vs perl 5.40.3, base-vs-fix-vs-perl three ways.
FOUR moved from DIFF to SAME and nothing regressed:
  01b  paren-less `open áº , â¦` / `close áº ` in a NON-strict file (the task's
       repro; under `use strict` the word is classified a CALL and
       `%p-fh-arg`'s macro-time rescue of `(pl-NAME)` was covering it, which
       is why the strict twin 01 was already right -- worth knowing)
  02   `print á» "â¦"` / `printf á» â¦` (wrong even under strict)
  03   `binmode á¸¤` / `fileno(á¸¤)`
  11   the package-QUALIFIED `open main::á»` / `print main::á»` / `<main::á»>`
Unchanged (the shapes the widening could have broken): a declared non-ASCII
uppercase SUB, a non-ASCII CONSTANT as a term (`áº  . "x"`, `áº  + 1`, `áº  / 2`,
`$a[áº  - 4]`), a fat-comma KEY, a class-name INVOCANT and method call, an
opendir/eof pair, and the no-strict bareword STRING (08c, the one the split
protects).

corpus-diff IDENTICAL over 111 + shapes.  Emission A/B vs a 0237940 worktree
over 923 files (lib 23 + perl t/ 605 + cpan-tests t/ 289 + shapes): exactly
TWO DIFF, 0 RCDIFF -- t/uni/readline.t (`open áº ,'+>',$file` / `close áº `:
`(p-open (p-void-ctx (|pl-áº |)) â¦)` -> `(p-open |áº | â¦)`) and t/uni/parser.t
(`opendir FÃÃ, "."` / `closedir FÃÃ`: the STRING "FÃÃ" and a CALL -> the
handle).  Gate-SET scan over BOTH populations (638x2): ZERO verdict moves --
the change is pure emission, it neither adds nor removes a refusal.

SUITE: NO row moves.  t/uni/readline.t stays 6/1 and t/uni/parser.t 28/30 --
the task's "expected mover" does NOT materialise, and the reason is worth
recording: readline.t's one remaining failure is row 1, `[perl #19566]`
(`eval { for (roref) { $_ = <FÊ> } }` must die "Modification of a read-only
value attempted"), a read-only-aliasing gap with nothing to do with the
bareword-handle family; and both files' `open`s sit under `use strict`, where
the call-plus-rescue path was already producing the right answer.  The fix is
a real one -- the four probes prove it -- it simply has no row behind it in
these two files.

RESIDUE: #852 (a CASELESS-script bareword handle, `open á, â¦`, is still
silently wrong in a non-strict file -- t/uni/readline.t line 31's own shape).

GUARDS: Pl/t/utf8-source-01.t 32 -> 36 rows (two positive, the ASCII inverse,
and the no-strict-string inverse the split protects), inverse-run on a
0237940 worktree: the two positives fail there, both inverses pass there.
The file's s456ag readline comment, which said the paren-less spelling "still
emits the STRING", was rewritten in the same commit (the s416 rule).
